chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
When a man says to his slave girl, 'I emancipate you and marry you, and I make your dower your emancipation,' then it is valid.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry his slave girl by making her emancipation her dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a specific contractual mechanism in Shia jurisprudence where a master emancipates his slave girl and marries her, designating the value of her freedom as her dowry (mahr). It highlights the flexibility of marital contracts in early Islamic law, allowing for the integration of manumission and marriage into a single legal transaction. The ruling underscores the principle that the emancipation itself serves as a valid consideration for the marriage contract.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba,
(It has been narrated) from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘When the man says to his slave girl, ‘I emancipate you and marry you, and make your dower to be your emancipation’, so it is allowed’.
